from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability", [
            "Conditional probability focuses on a reduced sample space.",
            "Think of it as zooming into event B.",
            "We only count outcomes where both A and B happen."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        sample_space = Rectangle(width=4, height=4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(sample_space, "B2", "E5")
        
        event_b = Ellipse(width=2.5, height=2, color="#FF9900", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(event_b, "B3", "D4")
        
        event_a = Ellipse(width=2, height=2.5, color="#00CCFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(event_a, "C2", "E3")
        
        intersection = Intersection(event_a, event_b, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        
        p_ab_label = MathTex("P(A|B)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(p_ab_label, "F4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sample_space))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF9900")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(event_b))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(event_a), FadeIn(intersection))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00CCFF")
        self.play(Write(p_ab_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Independence means knowing B gives no info on A.", "The probability of A remains unchanged by B.", "Visually, the ratio of A is constant throughout."]
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Independence", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show two coin flip outcomes
        coin1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        coin2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        label1 = Text("H", font_size=24).move_to(coin1)
        label2 = Text("T", font_size=24).move_to(coin2)
        coins = VGroup(VGroup(coin1, label1), VGroup(coin2, label2)).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(coins, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(coins))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display P(A|B) = P(A) formula
        formula = MathTex("P(A|B)", "=", "P(A)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate ratio of A remaining constant despite change in B
        # Represents the constant ratio using a bar chart
        bar_bg = Rectangle(height=2, width=3, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.2)
        bar_a = Rectangle(height=1, width=3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).align_to(bar_bg, DOWN)
        ratio_viz = VGroup(bar_bg, bar_a)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_viz, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(ratio_viz))
        # "Change" in B visually represented by shifting colors/movement
        self.play(bar_a.animate.set_color(GREEN), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem updates beliefs with new evidence.",
            "Think like a sniffer dog seeking truth.",
            "Start with a prior belief.",
            "Adjust it based on new likelihood data.",
            "Arrive at a refined posterior probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introducing Bayes' Theorem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        prior_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FFCC00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        prior_text = Text("Prior", font_size=18).move_to(prior_node)
        prior_group = VGroup(prior_node, prior_text)
        
        evidence_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        evidence_text = Text("Evidence", font_size=18).move_to(evidence_node)
        evidence_group = VGroup(evidence_node, evidence_text)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"P(H|E) = \frac{P(E|H)P(H)}{P(E)}", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        
        posterior_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.7)
        posterior_text = Text("Posterior", font_size=18).move_to(posterior_node)
        posterior_group = VGroup(posterior_node, posterior_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        self.place_at_grid(prior_group, "B2")
        self.play(Create(prior_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.place_at_grid(evidence_group, "B5")
        self.play(Create(evidence_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(formula, "D2", "D5")
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(posterior_node))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.place_at_grid(posterior_group, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(posterior_group))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Integration: When Bayes Meets Independence", [
            "Independence makes Bayesian calculations much simpler.",
            "Joint probabilities become simple products of individual terms.",
            "This acceleration is vital for real-time systems."
        ])
        
        # --- Formula objects ---
        # Using separate components for animation
        formula_joint = MathTex("P(", "A", ",", "B", "|", "D", ")", "=", "P(", "A", "|", "D", ")", "P(", "B", "|", "D", ",", "A", ")")
        formula_simple = MathTex("P(", "A", "|", "D", ")", "P(", "B", "|", "D", ")")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_joint, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_joint))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Transformation animation
        self.play(Transform(formula_joint, formula_simple))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        formula_joint.set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Independence simplifies computation significantly.", 
                         "Bayes' Theorem provides the logic for learning.", 
                         "Together, they power modern data classifiers."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application Loop", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show loop icon connecting Independence to Bayes
        loop = SVGMobject("icons/loop.svg") if False else Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FFCC00")
        loop_text = MathTex(r"Indep. \to Bayes").next_to(loop, UP)
        loop_group = VGroup(loop, loop_text)
        self.place_at_grid(loop_group, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(loop_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFCC00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate email filter nodes
        node1 = Dot(color="#00CCFF", radius=0.2)
        node2 = Dot(color="#00CCFF", radius=0.2)
        nodes = VGroup(node1, node2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        line = Line(node1.get_right(), node2.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        filter_group = VGroup(nodes, line)
        self.place_at_grid(filter_group, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(filter_group))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CCFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'Spam' or 'Ham' classification text
        label = Text("Spam / Ham", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly define Conditional Probability P(A|B) as focusing on a reduced sample space. Use a Venn diagram to visually show the 'slice' of A inside B.
sections.example: Visualizing a grid of 100 people; highlighting only those who own a dog (B) and then identifying the subset who also own a cat (A).

sections.title: The Concept of Independence
sections.content: Explain that events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate this as 'the presence of B does not change the ratio of A in the universe'.
sections.example: Flipping a coin twice: The result of the first flip does not change the 50/50 probability distribution of the second flip.

sections.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce the theorem as a mechanism to update beliefs (Posterior) based on new evidence (Likelihood). Use a 'Probability Tree' animation showing the flow from Prior to Posterior.
sections.example: A 'Medical Detective' scenario: Given a positive test result (Evidence), what is the actual probability of having the disease (Posterior)?

sections.title: Integration: When Bayes Meets Independence
sections.content: Show how independence simplifies the Likelihood calculation within Bayes' Theorem. Explain that when events are independent, the math simplifies from complex joint distributions to simple products.
sections.example: A robot sensor: If sensors A and B are independent, the probability of both detecting an obstacle is simply P(A) * P(B), making the Bayesian update much faster.

sections.title: Summary & Application Loop
sections.content: Summarize the core takeaway: Independence simplifies computation, while Bayes' Theorem provides the logic for learning from data.
sections.example: Applying the framework to an email spam filter: Independent keywords (words appearing independently) are used in a Bayesian classifier to label an email as 'Spam' or 'Ham'.
